status: Agreed selective header reading and compact retention; not implemented or cut over.

authorization.source: Direct human direction after section/memory-ceiling clarification
authorization.statement: Well then if we are well below 64 MB - then this limit is redundant? Only read the defined Header, parse the info we need, and only store that? Sorry I'm not a coder but that sounds good to me unless you disagree
authorization.interpretation: Accept the selective header/retention design and omit carrying over the historical accumulated-metadata buffer cap. This does not accept every pending layout/admission/recovery restriction.

agreedRules.readScope: For an eligible header read, use the safely established declared Header Metadata section and stop at its boundary.
agreedRules.extraction: Parse the agreed values plus only the temporary framing/type/ownership/reference context required to establish them. Skip unnecessary payloads by safe extent.
agreedRules.retention: Keep owned compact agreed results and necessary availability/format facts; release temporary header bytes, mappings and lookups after extraction. Do not retain a whole raw header/property graph or per-row raw copies.
agreedRules.old64MiBCap: Do not carry over the historical 64 MiB accumulated raw-metadata-buffer ceiling into this new design. There is no requirement to accumulate all recognised metadata into that old buffer.
agreedRules.bounds: Still validate declared header/file extents, packet/value lengths, arithmetic and supported typed forms before reading/allocating. No unchecked HeaderByteCount-sized allocation.
agreedRules.performance: Small sample size alone does not prove a universal maximum. Savings are expected from selective work/retention; no measured speed or memory result and no claim that removing a rarely reached check makes scanning faster.
agreedRules.separateScope: Closed/complete-only admission, byte-zero/run-in behavior, unsupported OP forms and footer/RIP recovery restrictions remain pending in the navigation review. Source-opening priorities, concurrency and cutover remain separate.

explicitConfirmations.statement: OK, let's lock that in for Bella. Is there anything else we need to decide for MXF before moving on to OMF?
explicitConfirmations.scope: Explicitly confirms selective defined-header reading, required-field extraction, compact retention/release and omission of the historical raw-buffer ceiling. Remaining unusual-layout/admission/recovery scope is not inferred as approved.
